title: Go SDK: streaming typed resume & deadline contract
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a new streaming contract for the Go SDK that provides typed resume semantics and clear deadline propagation rules. Current streaming behavior mixes context cancellation, per-request timeouts, and internal lease heartbeats in ways that are confusing to clients. Goals: 1) Define a minimal, ergonomic API that separates the stream lifecycle from request-level deadlines; 2) Ensure clients can safely resume interrupted streams when server-side partial state exists; 3) Make retry and backoff behavior explicit and testable; 4) Maintain backward compatibility with existing StreamReader/StreamWriter patterns where feasible.
background: We've had multiple incidents and customer tickets where long-running streaming sessions either leaked goroutines or failed to surface partial results when a transient network blip occurred. Existing tickets (ENG-447322, ENG-20458) implemented helpers for drain semantics but didn't provide a unified developer-facing contract. This work consolidates lessons into a single stream contract and implements it in the Go SDK with examples and tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New Stream type (StreamHandle) with explicit Open/Close/Resume methods documented in SDK reference
2) Context deadlines passed to Start/Send/Receive propagate to individual RPCs but do not forcibly close stream lifecycle unless CloseWithContext is called
3) Resume uses idempotency token + server-side resume token; client can attempt automatic resume up to N retries with jittered backoff
4) No goroutine leaks in simulated network partition tests (test harness validates), and telemetry increments for resumed vs fresh sessions
5) Examples in godoc and README demonstrating: a) short-lived per-message deadlines, b) long-lived stream with periodic heartbeats, c) graceful shutdown with partial flush
api_proposal: Start(ctx context.Context, opts StartOptions) error  // starts or resumes underlying RPC; ctx governs RPC deadline only
Send(ctx context.Context, msg *Message) error         // per-message deadline applies
Recv(ctx context.Context) (*Message, error)          // per-receive deadline applies
Pause() error                                        // client-driven pause without closing server lease
Resume(ctx context.Context) error                   // attempts resume using stored resume token
Close(ctx context.Context) error                    // graceful close; waits for server ack or timeout
CloseNow() error                                     // immediate teardown (no graceful flush)
StartOptions{ InitialResumeToken string, IdempotencyKey string, HeartbeatInterval time.Duration }

Semantics: ctx passed to Start/Resume/Send/Recv only applies to that underlying RPC call (deadline), not lifetime. To close the stream lifecycle, call Close or CloseNow. Pause leaves server-side lease alive for a short TTL to facilitate fast resume.
ergonomics_notes: Expose a small set of helpers: WithPerMessageTimeout(ctx, d), WithStreamLifetime(ctx, d) for users who want to bind lifetimes to contexts
Prefer returning well-typed errors: ErrStreamClosed, ErrResumeFailed, ErrDeadlineExceeded to make it easier for callers to decide retry logic
Provide a StreamController helper that coordinates graceful shutdown across multiple goroutines (example in examples/stream_controller.go)
implementation_notes: Server-side requirements: resume tokens and idempotency key must be supported by backend; if backend cannot resume, SDK falls back to fresh session if configured
Client-side will store last-known resume token in memory and optional persistence via StartOptions.InitialResumeToken
Retry policy: configurable policy with default: maxAttempts=3, baseBackoff=200ms, maxBackoff=2s, jitter=full. Resume retries use exponential backoff and reset on successful heartbeat
Heartbeats: SDK sends heartbeat pings when no messages are sent for HeartbeatInterval to keep KV cache/lease alive; heartbeat failures do not immediately close stream - they trigger resume attempts
Metrics: emit labels 'stream.start', 'stream.resume', 'stream.close', 'stream.resume_failed', 'stream.heartbeat_miss' with counts and latencies
testing_plan: Unit tests for Start/Resume/Close state machine (table-driven)
Integration tests against a simulated server that intentionally drops connections to validate resume path
Chaos test: kill connection mid-stream and ensure SDK resumes and delivers partial results where supported
Load test: create 1k concurrent streams with heartbeats enabled and verify CPU/memory bounds and no leaks
Goroutine leak detector enabled in CI for these tests
rollout_plan: 1) Merge API and tests behind feature flag (sdk-go-2.7.alpha_stream_resume)
2) Publish alpha client to internal artifact registry and run smoke tests with partner teams (Billing, Search)
3) Collect telemetry for 2 weeks and iterate on error semantics
4) Promote to GA in sdk-go-2.7 and update migration guide
5) Add examples to samples repo and a 'migrating from v1 stream' doc
risks: Backend resume/token semantics are required; if not implemented, UX degrades to best-effort and may confuse users
Incorrect context semantics could cause accidental stream lifetime closure if callers wrap top-level ctx incorrectly
Complexity of API may be overwhelming; we must keep helpers and patterns opinionated
Telemetry/billing changes required for resumed vs fresh sessions may need backend product sign-off
